name: Lower Gate Holonomy Is Carried by Split Squares
statement: In a two-sided passive gate-holonomy system from a dismantlable-ample terminal interval of order at most eleven, every shore on a directed lower-gate cycle has at least two concepts and carries a split-square marker. Thus the residual obstruction is a cyclic system of oriented split squares rather than arbitrary boundary subsets.
proof: For a cyclic shore $S$, its predecessor shore has a lower root blocked by $S$. The shore-root lemma puts one lower root in $S$, while the common-owner theorem puts a distinct non-root owner there, so $|S|\ge2$. Such a shore is proper in the residual set by construction. The contracted split-square marker theorem therefore applies to every cyclic shore.
